history.alt_text: Five-axle tractor-trailer straddling a weighbridge, its drive and trailer tandems cast in raking sunlight, measuring the legal axle spacing.
history.caption: A five-axle rig straddles a scale where one missing foot of wheelbase costs 2,500 pounds of legal payload.
history.title: Trailer-bridge weighbridge five-axle rig

style_when: scale is the story — a port, a refinery, a data centre hall, a rail yard, a skyline of cranes — and the reader needs to feel how big it is
prompt: 200mm telephoto compression of an unbranded five-axle tractor-trailer straddling a weighbridge at a container terminal loading bay. Low late-afternoon sun rakes from the left, casting long shadows of the twin axles and trailer bridge across asphalt and steel scale plates. Charcoal, safety yellow, and weathered orange palette; galvanized steel, concrete, and asphalt textures. Extreme asymmetric framing: the rear trailer tandem sits on the right third, the drive tandem in the middle distance, empty scale readout blurred at far left. Crystal-clear air, no fog, no people, no text.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, logos, readable numbers
rationale: The story is about scale, measurement, and the physical distance across a heavy freight truck. A compressed telephoto view makes the axle spacing and weighbridge legible while conveying industrial scale and the precision of the bridge formula.
cue: one foot of wheelbase is worth 2,500 pounds of freight
subject: a five-axle tractor-trailer straddling a weighbridge, its drive and trailer tandems aligned on the scale platform
core_thesis: A five-axle trailer loaded to exactly 80,000 pounds can still violate federal bridge formula because the 35-foot trailer bridge is one foot short of 36, and that missing foot costs 2,500 pounds of legal payload.
core_conflict: Legal weight capacity versus wheelbase spacing: the bridge formula turns a tape measure into a load limit, where one foot of spacing becomes 2,500 pounds of freight.
composition: Extreme asymmetric framing: rear trailer tandem on the right third, drive tandem in the middle distance, generous negative space above and left

review.depicts: A five-axle tractor-trailer with a red cab and silver box trailer sits on a concrete weighbridge platform, its three-axle trailer bogie filling the right side of the frame while a tall orange post holding a dark rectangular display screen stands at the left.
review.reason: The image shows the article's exact protagonist and mechanism — a five-axle rig with its tandem/bogie axles positioned on a weighbridge — so a reader would connect it directly to a story about axle spacing and scale weight limits.
